- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior high), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values or apply exponential decay filter.
